purpose: Modernize the legacy PHP web application while preserving workflow behavior, security, and data access outcomes.
intended_audience: Business analysts, product owners, delivery leads, and modernization engineering teams.
scope_in: Route surface: 785 web routes covering controller-managed operational workflows.
Presentation layer: 1,684 templates/views supporting dashboards, forms, and downstream notifications.

Model layer: 372 analyzed model file(s) were identified, and 1,684 view/template artifacts were detected in source inventory. The BRD appendices render a prioritized subset plus controller mappings, not the full presentation layer.
Data access layer: 3,836 SQL statements plus custom SQL functions and direct table access patterns requiring secure target-state migration.
Operational processing: 4 scheduled or async jobs, including GP import-style background integrations where present.
Application inventory: 249 controllers across staffing, onboarding, compliance, finance, and shared operational workflows.

Owner architecture overlay: MagicBox owner documentation claims 4,740 PHP files across 15 top-level folders and an explicit M01-M13 bounded-context taxonomy. The BRD crosswalk appendix reconciles current repo-evidenced coverage to that owner taxonomy.
scope_out: 4 detected adhoc_* staging or reporting tables, along with related OMS or ADP staging surfaces, remain out of current business-scope modernization unless they are explicitly promoted into scope.
Database trigger reimplementation and low-level data-function redesign remain out of the current BRD scope and are tracked through the data-function and target architecture decision path.
The GP import pipeline remains out of the current delivery scope until DEC-INTEGRATION-GP-001 is resolved.
SharePoint file operations remain out of the current delivery scope until DEC-INTEGRATION-SP-001 is resolved.
scope_note: The current BRD is grounded in 565,185 LOC across 3,827 files from the selected PHP scope. Unless the scope lock explicitly states full-repository coverage, this document should not be interpreted as claiming that every legacy workflow was analyzed.
assumptions: Route files and controllers represent the primary workflow entry points for the legacy web application.
Session, authentication, and SQL evidence require business validation where implementation logic is distributed across includes and templates.

The owner-provided MagicBox architecture document is used as an authoritative overlay for bounded contexts, report/messaging surfaces, and integration inventory, but it does not replace repo-evidenced controller and schema analysis.
Owner-domain tags shown on module entries are owner-overlay business classifications layered on top of controller-level implementation units.
constraints: Modernization must preserve route-level workflow behavior and security controls.
Inline SQL and session-coupled behavior must be re-designed into explicit target-state services and middleware.
scope_validation: Scope is derived from deterministic PHP route, controller, template, SQL, session, and auth extraction.
compliance_security_summary: Authentication, authorization, and session behavior must be preserved or intentionally redesigned with explicit approval.
Inline SQL and file upload/export behavior require security hardening during migration.
current_state_summary: Legacy PHP custom_php_mvc application with 785 routes, 249 controllers, 372 analyzed model files, 1684 templates/views, 3836 extracted SQL statements, and 4 detected background job workflows.
target_state_summary: Deliver a TypeScript-based target architecture with explicit services, route handling, and hardened security/data access behavior.
project_background: The legacy web application currently exposes 785 route-level workflows through 249 controllers, 372 analyzed model files, and 1684 templates/views.
Static extraction identified 3836 SQL statements plus session, authentication, background-job, and file I/O behavior that must be preserved or redesigned.
The modernization objective is to make route behavior, security controls, and validation logic explicit before build generation proceeds.

An owner-provided architecture document for MagicBox is being applied as a taxonomy overlay so bounded contexts, report depth, messaging surfaces, and third-party integrations remain visible even where controller-centric evidence is still shallow.
business_goals: Preserve business workflow outcomes for web routes and controller actions.
Externalize security, validation, and data access logic into target-state components.
Create an auditable modernization baseline for PHP route, template, and session behavior.
